options.text: \(f(x)\) is discontinuous in \([-1,1]\) and so has no maximum value or minimum value in \([-1,1]\)
\(f(x)\) is continuous in \([-1,1]\) and so has maximum value and minimum value
\(f(x)\) is discontinuous in \([-1,1]\) but still has the maximum and minimum value
\(f(x)\) is bounded in \([-1,1]\) and does not attain maximum or minimum value

solution.text:
Hint : \(f(x)= \begin{cases}x+1 & -1 \leq x \leq 0 \\ -x & 0 < x \leq 1\end{cases}\) \(\left.\begin{array}{l}f\left(-1^{-}\right)=0 \\ f(-1)=0 \\ f\left(-1^{+}\right)=0\end{array}\right]\) continuous at \(x=-1\) \(\left.\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{f}(0)=1 \\ \mathrm{f}\left(0^{-}\right)=1 \\ \mathrm{f}\left(0^{+}\right)=0\end{array}\right]\) discontinuous at \(\mathrm{x}=0\)
obviously \(f(x)\) has local maximum at \(x=0\)
